injuries.summary:
**Today's NFL injury briefing**

**Status changes**
- **Malik Nabers (Giants WR)**: Worked with trainers to start practice, then moved into team work. He’s now **day to day**, with his workload varying day to day. This is a step up from mostly individual drills earlier in camp.
  - **Why it matters:** Big impact on the Giants’ passing game and fantasy.
- **Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson (Bears CBs)**: Both are **day to day** with their injuries.
  - **Why it matters:** Chicago’s secondary remains in flux.
- **Kendre Miller**: Left practice early with athletic trainers.
  - **Why it matters:** Status unclear; worth monitoring for any missed practice time.
- **Lorenzo Styles**: Placed on **IR**.
  - **Why it matters:** He’s out for the near term; no injury detail was specified.
- **Tyler Batty**: Tore his ACL, which helped prompt the Vikings’ signing of **Kyle Van Noy** for edge depth.
  - **Why it matters:** Minnesota’s edge rotation had been thin.

**Returning from injury**
- **George Kittle**: He’s 8 months removed from an Achilles tear. No current status update was specified.
- **Mason Graham (Browns DT)**: Entering Year 2 healthier after playing through a broken rib as a rookie.

**Watch next**
- Nabers’ practice load.
- Any update on Miller after leaving with trainers.
- Whether the Bears’ cornerbacks move past day-to-day status.
- How Minnesota’s edge depth looks after Batty’s ACL tear.

That makes Skattebo the most fantasy-relevant Giants back to track, with Harris the main threat to his early-down share. [1]

- **Malachi Fields (WR)** — He projects ahead of Darius Slayton on the current depth chart, and the note says Fields was the Giants’ highest-graded receiver this preseason with strong contested-catch results. That puts Fields in the mix for outside snaps and makes Slayton a name to watch if the rotation keeps shifting. [1]

- **Likely (TE)** — The Giants are planning to deploy him as a big slot receiver, not just a traditional tight end. That kind of alignment usually points to more routes and easier target access, which would boost his reception upside if the role sticks. [1]

- **Brian Burns (EDGE)** — Burns is coming off a 16.5-sack season, and John Harbaugh said he can excel in Dennard Wilson’s defense; the note also says Abdul Carter’s continued development should keep Burns from seeing many double-teams. For IDP, that’s a favorable setup for another productive sack season. [5]

PHI.summary:
- **Makai Lemon (WR)** — The rookie the Eagles expected to contribute right away got his first preseason run, catching 3 of 5 targets for 3 yards while also being targeted on Tanner McKee’s interception and muffing a punt. The bigger note is role-related: Philadelphia wants to get Lemon in the slot, and the team is treating the rough debut as a speed-up-from-injury issue rather than a depth-chart setback. [1, 7]

- **Jaydon Blue (RB)** — Blue is on Philadelphia’s practice squad, and SI flagged him as a candidate to become an extra running back on game days. That keeps him on the radar as a pass-catching depth stash behind Saquon Barkley, especially given his college receiving profile. [4, 6]

- **Tanner McKee (QB) and Andy Dalton (QB)** — The Eagles still have not named a backup quarterback, with McKee and Dalton “still battling it out” for QB2. That matters mainly as injury insurance for Jalen Hurts, but it’s still a real depth-chart competition heading into Week 1. [5]

- **Nick Sirianni / Sean Mannion (coach/OC)** — Philadelphia has leaned on extra “call-it” periods in practice to give first-time play-caller Sean Mannion and the offensive staff more live, game-speed reps. It’s a scheme/prep signal more than a usage change, but it suggests the Eagles are trying to smooth out operational issues before the regular season. [8]

SEA.summary:
- **Jadarian Price (RB)** — Seattle is expected to feature the rookie first-rounder heavily in the Week 1 run game against New England, and he should get the bulk of the carries as he gets healthier after missing preseason work. Sam Darnold also described him as a versatile back who can handle targets and screens, so Price looks like the clear fantasy winner in this backfield to open the season. [9]

- **Seahawks offensive line** — Brandon Thorn moved Seattle up to No. 10 in his offensive line ranking, which the item says bodes well for Jadarian Price. That’s not a usage change, but it is a positive efficiency signal for the run game and supports Price’s weekly ceiling if the line holds up. [12]

- **Jason Myers (K)** — Myers went 4-for-9 on kicks in the preseason, including 2-for-5 on field goals and 2-for-4 on extra points, and cost Seattle 7.4 expected points according to TruMedia. The article stops short of panic, but it’s the one fantasy-kicker note to monitor if the misses carry into September. [3]
